QuestionStmt.S: If the velocity of the electron in Bohr's first orbit is $2.19 \times 10^6$ m/s, calculate the de Broglie wavelength associated with it. ($h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}$ J s and mass of electron = $9.10938 \times 10^{-31}$ kg)

Solution.S:
The de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{h}{mv}$.

Given: $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}$ J s, $m = 9.10938 \times 10^{-31}$ kg, $v = 2.19 \times 10^6$ m/s.

$$\lambda = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{(9.10938 \times 10^{-31})(2.19 \times 10^6)} = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{1.9949 \times 10^{-24}} = 3.32 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$$

Converting to picometres: $3.32 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m} = 332 \text{ pm}$.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{332 \text{ pm}}$$

Hence, the correct option is A.
